title: Tides and the Moon
examples: What causes the ocean water to move in and out?
Are the tides caused by the sun or the moon?
What is the difference between spring and neap tides?

explain.say: The moon has a gravitational pull on Earth.

draw.text: Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's water.

explain.say: This pull makes the water on the side of Earth facing the moon bulge out.
Because of the moon's pull, we usually have two high tides each day.
Spring tides happen when the sun, moon, and earth line up.

draw.text: Sun, Moon, Earth align for Spring Tides.

explain.say: Neap tides happen when the sun and moon pull at right angles.

draw.text: Sun and Moon pull at right angles.

explain.say: In real life, think about the ocean water filling a bay.

draw.text: Bay water level changes with tides.

faq.a: Tides are mainly caused by the gravitational pull of the moon on Earth's oceans. The sun also plays a role, but the moon has the biggest effect.
asks: What makes the water move in and out?
Is it just the moon doing this?

faq.q: How many tides do we get in a day?
faq.a: Generally, we experience two high tides and two low tides every single day. This cycle repeats regularly.
asks: Does the number of tides change?

faq.a: Spring tides happen when the sun, moon, and earth are lined up. This causes the biggest difference between high and low tides.
Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at a right angle to each other. This results in smaller differences between high and low tides.

faq.q: Does the sun cause tides too?
faq.a: Yes, the sun's gravity pulls on Earth's water too. However, the moon's pull is usually stronger, making it the main cause.
asks: Is the sun important for tides?

facts: The moon's gravity pulls on the Earth's oceans.
Most locations experience two high tides and two low tides daily.
Spring tides happen when the sun, moon, and earth align.
Neap tides happen when the sun and moon are at right angles.

quiz.say: What force primarily causes the ocean tides?

options.show: The Earth spinning on its axis.
options.say: The Earth spinning on its axis.

quiz.why: The moon's gravity is the main force pulling the Earth's water.

wrong.0: Wind causes waves, but not the predictable, large-scale tides.
wrong.2: This causes day and night, but not the regular tide changes.
wrong.3: The sun's pull is strong, but the moon's pull is usually stronger.

quiz.say: When are the tides at their strongest?

options.show: When the sun is at its highest.
options.say: When the sun is at its highest.

quiz.why: Alignment of the three bodies creates the strongest tidal pull.

wrong.0: The sun's position alone does not guarantee the strongest tide.
wrong.2: Full moon is one time, but the alignment is what matters.
wrong.3: New moon is another time, but the alignment is what matters.

quiz.say: If the sun and moon are at a right angle, what kind of tides happen?
quiz.why: A right angle means the pulls work against each other, making the tides smaller.

wrong.0: This does not describe the pattern of the water level.
wrong.1: Gravity always causes some tidal effect.
wrong.3: Spring tides require the three bodies to line up together.
